newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu eases, c.bank starts to drain dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu eases, c.bank starts to drain dlrs.

text.p: Romania's leu currency edged down to 6,900/7,100 to the dollar in late trading on Thursday, after earlier firming to 6,700/7,000, as the central bank (BNR) rejoined trading and soaked up excess dollars, traders said.

"The BNR was in the market at the close but one cannot talk about a typical intervention. At mid-day it accepted offers coming from banks which wanted to get rid of their dollar surpluses," said a trader with a state-run bank.
"It (BNR) drained dollars at rates close to 7,000 lei, consequently halting a downward pressure on the greenback," said a trader with a foreign bank in Bucharest.
BNR officials declined to confirm any moves on Thursday.

"The central bank is monitoring the market step by step. It is ready for any intervention either on the selling or the buying side but we will not reveal its short-term intentions," BNR spokesman Adrian Vasilescu told Reuters.

Over the past three days the BNR stopped its months-long practice to mop up funds from a market where dollar supply was constantly higher than demand due to growing foreign inflows following higher interest in Romanian equities.
As a result the leu rose to 6,700/7,000 to the dollar early on Thursday from about 7,000/120 on Wednesday and lows of 7,280/330 two weeks ago.

Dealers suggested the BNR move to stop dollar purchases aimed to limit leu liquidity injection on a money market where short-term rates dropped rapidly to 50 percent from some 190 percent in early April.
They said the leu's future trends were depending on the BNR's action to mop up dollar surplus as hard currency demand was low with importers still reluctant to join trading.
Traders earlier said any further upsurge in the leu might hurt exporters as well as a short-term reluctance from foreign investors investing in Romanian equities.
